title: Evaluation Framework for AI Systems in “the Wild”

bias_targets.methodology: The paper outlines a conceptual framework suggesting the curation of real-world evaluation data to account for performance variations and unintended impacts across racial subgroups, rather than conducting an empirical measurement itself.
The paper outlines a conceptual framework suggesting the curation of real-world evaluation data to account for performance variations and unintended impacts across gender subgroups.

To address biases where LLMs acting as evaluators prefer certain styles of output (or their own generated outputs), the framework recommends verifying automated scores against human judgments and using multiple different LLMs for the evaluation.

In the context of content moderation, the paper proposes evaluating models by analyzing their performance across different demographic groups to ensure marginalized voices are not disproportionately silenced or misrepresented.
